source_matching_peer_consumed.use: Avoided duplicating the arbitrary-pivot physical-row 1<p<2 theorem; optimized it to an explicit sqrt(ell log(1/ell)) interval bound.

partner_result_applied.actual_application: Combined the exact Fejer convolution kernel with the new all-finite-Lp zero-pivot theorem to prove sup_y D_T <= p M (T/(2pi M))^(1/p), optimized to logarithmic growth.

new_results.statement: If X is independent of (U,R), f_X<=1, p_U<=M and T=2XU+R with arbitrary dependence between U and R, then ||p_T||_p <= p M^(1-1/p) for every finite p>1.
For intervals of length ell with M ell<=e^-2, P(T in I)<=e M ell log(1/(M ell)).
For the signed Fejer quantity of account04/B01, sup_y D_T<=p M (T/(2pi M))^(1/p); in particular <=e M log(T/(2pi M)) when T/(2pi M)>=e^2.

For iid Uniform[-1/2,1/2], 2XU has density log(1/(2|t|)) and D_T(0)=log T+O(1); a single zero bilinear row cannot yield uniform signed-Fejer control. This has only two large eigenvalues and is not a target counterexample.

With iid Uniform[-1/2,1/2], a=1 and R=U^2, T=(X+U)^2 has density (1-sqrt(y))/sqrt(y), not in L2; the arbitrary-pivot row theorem cannot be upgraded to p=2 from row hypotheses alone. Not a target counterexample.

unresolved_implication: Spend the simultaneously retained third-direction/residual disjoint-pair resource jointly with the physical-row estimate before logarithmic signed-Fejer growth develops; a one-row endpoint alone is now proved insufficient.
next_step: In the exact-rank-three near-isotropic/overlap-one branch, build a grouped two-resource inequality coupling row shear with residual disjoint-pair mass without factorizing dependent spectral coordinates.
